Anshul Kamboj | PoTM: [On the key to his outstanding figures of 2 for 22 in 10 overs] I think the key was just consistent length and line, not thinking about how the wicket is behaving, just the basic plan, bowling on right lines and right areas. [On using variations in seam position] I think the wobble seam ball was working very well, so I was using that again and again. [On his preparations for the series] Just working on lengths and good lines, and just looking at the strengths and weaknesses of the batsmen and just working on that. [On adjusting his length to the conditions in New Zealand] No, it doesn't matter, because I also get a good amount of bounce off the wicket as well. So it's like it's only about the length which I am bowling, just focusing on that. [On assessing conditions at different venues] You just have to look at the wicket and see what is happening on the wicket, what is the best ball to bowl, what is the right length to bowl, just focus on that.

Mitchell Santner | New Zealand captain: [On New Zealand's batting performance] Yeah, I think the pitch probably bounced and, you know, it was probably a little bit faster than we kind of expected at Eden Park. I think we just probably didn't adapt as quick as we could. And with some good bowling from India as well. [On the challenge of adapting to the bounce at Eden Park] Yeah, I think when you try to fight the bounce at Eden Park, it can be quite hard. I think the way they kind of used it a little bit more and, Shreyas was trying to go more fine with the shorter balls. And yeah, obviously bounced a lot and after the rain it kind of skidded on nicely. So yeah, a few short balls out there. [On the bowling unit's response after a difficult start] Yeah, very happy. It was easy for us to kind of roll over there after the start they got. So credit to the fast bowlers to keep backing it up. So yeah, I think we found some good stuff at the end of the game there and we can kind of go on to Wellington.
